profile.summary: Graphinity predicts the change in antibody-antigen binding affinity caused by a mutation, the quantity written as delta delta G. It takes the structures of the wild-type complex and of the mutant, builds an atomic graph around the mutated site in each, passes both through an equivariant graph neural network, subtracts the two embeddings and reads out one number. The authors report Pearson correlations up to 0.87 on 645 experimental single-point mutations, then show that this reflects overtraining on a few hundred data points rather than a generalisable model. To find out how much data would be needed they built synthetic sets of 942,723 FoldX and 20,829 Rosetta Flex ddG values, and conclude that orders of magnitude more experimental data are likely required, with diversity mattering as well as volume.
profile.summary_source_locator: README: title, Abstract and Synthetic ddG Datasets; paper: Methods, EGNN architecture

summary_quotes.text: Here we present Graphinity, an equivariant graph neural network architecture built directly from antibody–antigen structures that achieves test Pearson’s correlations of up to 0.87 on experimental change in binding affinity (ΔΔG) prediction.
However, our model, like previous methods, appears to be overtraining on the few hundred experimental data points available and performance is not robust to train–test cut-offs.

We generated synthetic ∆∆G datasets by mutating the interfaces of structurally-resolved complexes from SAbDab (Dunbar et al., 2014; Schneider et al., 2021) using FoldX (942,723 mutations; Schymkowitz et al., 2005) and Rosetta Flex ddG (20,829 mutations; Barlow et al., 2018).

For ΔΔ<italic toggle="yes">G</italic> prediction, we generated and aggregated graphs of the WT and mutant structures. Both graphs were fed through the three <italic toggle="yes">E</italic>(<italic toggle="yes">n</italic>) EGC layers and the resulting embeddings subtracted from one another (WT − Mutant) before the last linear layer.
Our results indicate that there are currently insufficient experimental data to accurately and robustly predict ΔΔG, with orders of magnitude more likely needed.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: A structure goes in as a PDB file and becomes an atomic graph: non-hydrogen atoms are nodes, pairs of atoms less than 4 angstroms apart are edges, node features are a one-hot LibMolGrid atom type and edge features say whether the edge is within one binding partner or between the two. The graph is cut down to the neighbourhood of the mutated site: atoms on the mutated chain within 4 angstroms of the mutated residue, plus atoms on the partner chain within 4 angstroms of those. The network is three E(n) equivariant graph convolutional layers with a hidden dimension of 128. For a delta delta G prediction, the wild-type and mutant graphs are each passed through those layers and the embeddings subtracted, wild type minus mutant, before a final linear layer. Training used mean squared error, Adam at learning rate 0.001, batch size 32, dropout 0.2 on edges, weight decay 1e-16 and global max pooling as readout, for 500 epochs except on the large FoldX set where 10 epochs were used for cost.

quotes.text: Our model is composed of three <italic toggle="yes">E</italic>(<italic toggle="yes">n</italic>) equivariant graph convolutional (EGC) layers<sup><xref ref-type="bibr" rid="CR23">23</xref></sup> with a hidden dimension of 128.
generates an atomic-resolution graph with nodes representing non-hydrogen atoms and edges representing interactions between nodes <4 Å apart.
The node features are a one-hot encoded vector describing the LibMolGrid atom type
The models were trained with mean squared error loss.
optimizer, Adam; learning rate, 0.001; batch size, 32; dropout, 0.2

Models were trained using PyTorch Lightning for 500 epochs, with the exception of the synthetic FoldX ΔΔ<italic toggle="yes">G</italic> dataset models, which, due to the high computational costs, were trained for 10 epochs.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There is no single released Graphinity model. The repository ships eight checkpoints from the data volume experiment, under example/ddg_synthetic/FoldX/varying_dataset_size/model_weights, each about 4.3 MB and named by the number of FoldX training examples it saw: subset_580, subset_900, subset_4500, subset_9000, subset_45000, subset_90000, subset_450000 and full_848597. They are illustrations of the data scaling question rather than a production predictor, so a result must name the checkpoint. The repository also keeps the experimental delta delta G datasets with their ten-fold cross-validation splits at CDR sequence identity cut-offs of 100, 90 and 70 per cent and a random split, under data/ddg_experimental. The environment is pinned hard, to Python 3.7.10, PyTorch 1.8.0 and PyTorch Geometric 1.6.3, with and without CUDA 10.2.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Supervised regression model for change in antibody-antigen binding affinity, built as an equivariant graph neural network over atomic structure.

quotes.text: ## Graphinity: Equivariant Graph Neural Network Architecture for Predicting Change in Antibody-Antigen Binding Affinity
We developed a deep learning EGNN architecture to predict change in antibody–antigen binding affinity

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Three E(n) equivariant graph convolutional layers with hidden dimension 128, global max pooling and a final linear layer, applied to wild-type and mutant graphs whose embeddings are subtracted. The authors call it modular and easily adapted to other tasks.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Experimental models: the AB-Bind dataset of 645 single-point mutations from 29 complexes, called Experimental_ddG_645, with variants including and excluding reverse mutations and non-binders. The repository also carries a second experimental set of 608 mutations. Synthetic models: 942,723 FoldX delta delta G values and 20,829 Rosetta Flex ddG values, generated by mutating the interfaces of structurally resolved complexes from SAbDab. The checkpoint named full_848597 reflects the subset actually used for its training run.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: Set by the graph construction rather than a sequence length: only atoms within 4 angstroms of the mutated residue on its own chain, plus atoms on the partner chain within 4 angstroms of those, enter the graph. Whole complexes are not embedded.

run_guide.summary: Build the pinned conda environment and run the bundled five-mutation inference example.
prerequisites: Conda, and Python 3.7.10 as the environment recipe pins it.
No GPU required: the authors state Graphinity can be run without one and give a CUDA-free environment recipe.
Linux or Mac, the platforms the authors say it has been tested on. Their paper results used one NVIDIA RTX 6000 GPU and four CPUs.
BSD 3-Clause terms for the code. The checkpoints are committed in the same repository, with no separate licence statement.

git clone https://github.com/oxpig/Graphinity.git
cd Graphinity
git checkout --detach 281a72fde123d89bf29a50a73fc787f5d355e1b9

limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The example runs on FoldX-generated structures; predicting for your own mutation means producing a mutant structure first and writing a configuration file for it.
The pinned stack is old, so the install may fail on current hardware or CUDA versions; the README gives a reinstall order for the PyTorch Geometric packages when it does.

notes: The record came from the antibody-antigen affinity evaluation framework (existing source lit-interactions-20261011-mochibind-source-isci2026). Graphinity is as much a study of data requirements as a model: the shipped weights are the data volume experiment's checkpoints, trained on FoldX-generated values, and the authors' own conclusion is that the available experimental data are insufficient for a generalisable predictor. Anyone citing a Graphinity number should say which checkpoint and which train-test cut-off, since the paper's own headline correlation of 0.87 is presented as evidence of overtraining. The repository holds the experimental datasets with their ten-fold cross-validation splits, and prediction CSVs for the synthetic data volume runs, but no checkpoint trained on experimental data. No saved file states a licence for the committed checkpoints, so weights_licence is null; the repository itself is BSD 3-Clause.
